title: fix(dashboard): a global filter on a multi-value field is sent as $contains, not = / $in
body:

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XP3RHGWUG7UH3fNa4tBa9UC)_

repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5okniknzVVR3KTSVr1 — os-dev, area a4-D, route A per seat note 7066557346. The other half of this card, the condition editors, merged before this PR opened (PR #36165), so this PR closes the card.

## 维护者速读

- 仪表盘查看者按「项目标签」「团队成员」这类可多选的字段筛选时，图表和指标现在显示匹配的数据，之前显示为 0。
- 属于「仪表盘与条件编辑器在多值字段上发出服务器拒收的筛选」这张卡的后一半（前一半条件编辑器已合并），替仪表盘查看者解决筛选后空白的问题。
- 出错时查看者会看到部件先短暂显示加载占位再出数；读不到字段定义时退回旧行为并在控制台提示；本改动可直接撤回。
- 无

## What changes

A dashboard `select` / `lookup` global filter bound to a field that holds several values (`multiple: true` on a select, lookup or user field, or a `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` field) was sent as `field = value`, or `$in` for several values. The server refuses both there (data door 400 `INVALID_FILTER`; dataset door 200 with count 0). It is now sent as `{ field: { $contains: value } }`, and several values as `$or` over one `$contains` each.

- **`@object-ui/types`** — `DataSource.getDataset?(datasetName, { callerPackage })`: an optional read of a dataset definition. It resolves `null` when no dataset of that name is served, and a failed read rejects.
- **`@object-ui/data-objectstack`** — `ObjectStackAdapter.getDataset` reads `GET /api/v1/meta/dataset/NAME` through `client.meta.getItem`. It sends the reader's package as `callerPackage`, answers `null` for the item-less envelope and for a 404, rejects on any other failure, and caches the answer per name and package.
- **`@object-ui/core`** — `buildWidgetScopedFilter` takes an optional fifth argument: per bound field, the operators the field takes when it is stored as a JSON column. A member filter on such a field becomes `$contains` / `$or`. A member filter on a structured JSON field (`json`, `address`: no `contains`) keeps `=` / `$in`, as before. New export `boundMemberFilterNames`. Nothing changes for callers that do not pass the argument.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`** — new `filterFieldFacts.ts`. When the dashboard declares a `select` / `lookup` filter, `DashboardRenderer` reads each widget's object: a dataset-bound widget's `Dataset.object` through `getDataset`, or a `provider: 'object'` widget's own `object`. It then reads the object's fields through `getObjectSchema` and gets the operators from `jsonColumnFilterOperators`, the helper the list quick filter and the filter builder already use, so no second operator table exists. While the definition is in flight, a widget bound by an active member filter draws a skeleton and sends no query. When the definition cannot be read, the old `=` / `$in` lowering stays and a console warning names the filter, the source and the reason, once.
- Docs: `content/docs/frontend/data-source.mdx` documents `getDataset`, and the plugin-dashboard README documents the lowering.

Read first, by risk:

1. `ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DashboardRenderer.tsx`, the hunk around `holdForFieldFacts`. This is where a widget's query is held. A wrong condition here would hold a widget forever or send `=` first.
2. `ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/filterFieldFacts.ts`, `useFilterFieldFacts`. The effect is keyed on joined source keys, never on an array identity (ui AGENTS.md #10). A source that cannot be asked answers `unavailable` synchronously, so a data source without `getDataset` is never held.
3. `ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts`, `buildJsonColumnMemberClause`. The `$contains` / `$or` shape.

## Tests

<details><summary>New pins (4 files, 34 tests), head 5a0b3c97</summary>

- `ui/packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/dashboard-filters.multiValue-35992.test.ts` (12 tests): one member gives `$contains`; several give `$or`; a one-member list gives no one-arm `$or`; a multi-value lookup/user; an explicit `filterBindings` target; a single-value field keeps `=` / `$in`; a text filter is unchanged; AND with other filters; no operator answer keeps `=` / `$in`; a structured JSON field keeps `=` / `$in`, explicit binding included, with no warning (round 2); `boundMemberFilterNames`.
- `ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/filterFieldFacts.multiValue-35992.test.ts` (8 tests): real field definitions through `jsonColumnFilterOperators` cover a multiselect, a select/lookup/user with `multiple: true`, and single-value select/lookup unchanged. A field the object does not declare keeps `=`. Covers pending and unavailable facts, and the widget source (dataset, `provider: 'object'` under `data` and under `options.data`, inline rows).
- `ui/packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DashboardRenderer.multiValueFilter-35992.test.tsx` (8 tests), the fixture dashboard: a global filter bound to `labels` (multiselect) and `team_members` (user, `multiple: true`). It checks `runtimeFilter` is `$contains` and that no query ever carried `labels = frontend`. The query is held behind a skeleton until `getDataset` answers. No hold while the filter is empty. A single-value field keeps `=`. With no `getDataset`, or a dataset that is not served, `=` is kept and the filter is named in a warning. A `provider: 'object'` table gets the same `$contains` in its `find` `$filter`.
- `ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/getDataset-35992.test.ts` (6 tests, real `ObjectStackClient` over a stubbed fetch): the route, `callerPackage`, the item-less envelope gives `null`, a 404 gives `null`, a 500 rejects with its `httpStatus` and `code`, one read per name.
</details>

<details><summary>Affected suites and type-check, head 5a0b3c97</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard run type-check`: all four printed `type-check: Done`.
- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/ packages/data-objectstack/ packages/types/`: Test Files 836 passed (836), Tests 15976 passed, 6 skipped (15982), VERDICT command-exit 0.

</details>

<details><summary>Reverse verification</summary>

At 9d286428 the four source files were restored to base 146b6f9b (`dashboard-filters.ts`, core `index.ts`, `DashboardRenderer.tsx`, data-objectstack `index.ts`) with the new tests and `filterFieldFacts.ts` kept. Result: Test Files 4 failed (4), Tests 23 failed, 11 passed (34). The 11 that stay green are the single-value controls, the source classification and the pending/unavailable facts, which do not depend on the restored files. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`: `git diff HEAD` was empty, and each `git hash-object` matched its HEAD blob. Tests resolve `@object-ui/*` to `src` through the ui vitest alias, so no dist rebuild was involved.
</details>

<details><summary>Live measurement, showcase (SqlDriver), fresh backend on a random port, torn down after</summary>

`showcase_project` has 5 rows. Labels were set on 3 of them: `[frontend, qa]`, `[frontend]` and `[qa]`.

- `GET /api/v1/meta/dataset/showcase_project_metrics` returns item `object` = `showcase_project`. In the object definition, `labels` is `multiselect` and `team_members` is `user` with `multiple: true`. The built adapter's `getDataset` returned `showcase_project` for it, and `null` for a name that does not exist (404).
- Dataset door `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query`, `project_count`: `{labels: frontend}` returns 0; `$in [frontend, qa]` returns 0; `$contains frontend` returns 2; `$or` of two `$contains` returns 3; that `$or` inside an `$and` returns 3.
- Data door `POST /api/v1/data/showcase_project/query`: `=` and `$in` return 400 `INVALID_FILTER`; `$contains` returns 2; the `$or` returns 3.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The filter bar's select control picks one value, so the `$or` (any of several) arm is reached only when a filter variable holds a list, as a programmatic value. It is pinned at the unit level. The rendered fixture covers the single-member case on a dataset widget and on a `provider: 'object'` table.
- A filter bound to a relationship path on a dataset (`account.region`) is not looked up through the relationship. The base object does not declare that name, so it keeps `=` / `$in` with no warning. No multi-value field behind a to-one path was measured.
- `DashboardGridLayout` was not changed. It applies no dashboard filters today.
- The dataset door answers `=` / `$in` on a JSON column with 200 and count 0 instead of refusing. That is #36168's, and it is not changed here.
- carrier: none · noted · a `select` / `lookup` filter bound to a structured JSON field (`json`, `address`, empty checks only) keeps the `=` / `$in` lowering it had before this PR, explicit bindings included. The server refuses that filter or answers it with no rows, so the widget shows no data under it. Changing that is outside this card (round 2, L1-b comment 7068252699).

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DashboardRenderer.multiValueFilter-35992.test.tsx` should report 8 passed. Then delete the `jsonColumnOperatorsFor(fieldFacts)` argument in `DashboardRenderer.tsx` and run the file again: the `$contains` cases fail and receive `{ labels: 'frontend' }`.
